evidence_quotes: Pay Increases for Public School Employees:

For the fiscal year 2013-2016, pay increases are mandated for public school employees. The increases are as follows:

- For the 2013-14 fiscal year: up to a 5% increase.
- For the 2014-15 and 2015-16 fiscal years: up to a 2.5% increase each year.

The increases are in addition to any step increases already due to employees.

Special Considerations:

- Employees should receive full credit for prior public school experience.
- No pay reductions or changes in work hours can be made because of these pay raises.
- Local boards have the option to exclude part-time community education and child care program employees from these provisions.

The bill also provides COLAs for retirees:

- For retirees with an effective date prior to October 1, 2012: a 5% increase in benefits starting October 1, 2013.
- For retirees with an effective date prior to October 1, 2013: a 2.5% increase starting October 1, 2014.
- For retirees with an effective date prior to October 1, 2014: another 2.5% increase starting October 1, 2015.

These adjustments are not applicable if the retiree is receiving Medicaid benefits or if their eligibility for Medicaid would be affected by the increase.

Miscellaneous Provisions:

- The pay raises do not apply to superintendents unless approved by a majority vote of the governing body.
- Career-Technical Programs are protected from any reductions due to these pay increases.
- Local salary supplements, bonuses for certifications, and federal portions of JROTC instructor salaries are excluded from these provisions.
